text: Program architecture: how a doeff program is built, and how it runs.
A program is a value. It is control instructions, a DoExpr, that the Rust VM evaluates.
An effect is plain data. It is dispatched at one place only: Perform.
Calling an at-do function runs nothing. It returns a program, and the body has not run yet.
An effect such as Ask key is a value too. It names an operation, and does nothing by itself.
Yield Ask is lowered to yield Perform of Ask. Both reach the same handler, and both get ada.
run takes that one program, and returns its raw value.
Handler installers take a program and return a program. Calling them nests the handlers.
h2 is innermost, and sees every effect first. It answers Greet.
Lookup is not for h2. It passes outward, and h1 answers it.
Save passes h2 and h1, and reaches h0, the outermost. Dispatch always goes from inside out.
The VM runs the program one step at a time. A program that yields a program calls it.
Each call becomes a frame in the VM, with its function, file and line.
When charge raises, the doeff traceback lists the chain of calls, and the yield each one waits at.
To watch the effects, wrap a program in WithObserve, with an observer.
The observer is called with each effect dispatched in the body: Ask, Get, Put and Tell.
The answer is still forty two. Tell start is outside the body, so the observer does not see it.
run has no trace flag. Observation composes into the program, like a handler.
Async programs run under the scheduler: run of scheduled of the program.
The scheduler is a handler. It answers Spawn and Gather, and switches tasks at each wait.
Two tasks interleave, a1, b1, a2, b2, inside the VM's one step loop, and run returns both results.
Without scheduled, Spawn finds no handler, and the run raises UnhandledEffect.
Programs are values. Effects are data, dispatched at Perform. Handlers nest, and the VM steps it all. That is how doeff runs algebraic effects.
